summary: Tested the noise-pattern hardening in mpa.js (compileNoise/noiseRules/stripNoise) using the production-like private admin lists. I created them through the admin API: 'Admin - Food Synonyms' has 1. Salt / 2. Tomatoes / 4. Pepper groups with indented items, and 'Admin - Food Noise Words' has the full production list including '(.*)', '.*' and '[a-z]+'. GET /api/mpa/rules returned 14 synonym items (11 indented) and 25 noise items. Node unit check (/app/tests/mpa_bidir_unit.mjs, extended): 27/28 pass. The 11 tests from iteration 59 still pass. The synonym map is built with 12 keys, so '(.*)' no longer wipes names. '(.*)' compiles to the span /\(.*?\)/gi. '.*', '[a-z]+' and '(oops' are skipped. All requested pairs match. Exact matches show the solid badge, and the non-food area gives no badge. 1 edge-case failure: a comma inside brackets (see below). UI on the Pro boat (Playwright, aisles unticked, provisions mocked): P1: 'Salt 1 tsp' -> dashed sub badge 'Sea Salt · Galley Cupboard 1'. 'Tomatoes (finely chopped) 200g' -> 'Tinned plum tomatoes 400g'. 'Ground black pepper' -> 'White Pepper'. 'Fresh peas 200g' -> 'Frozen peas'. '2 Crisps' -> solid mpa-onboard badge, 'Crisps – 5 · 1 on board' (6 minus 1). P2: 'Sea salt 1 tsp' -> sub badge 'Salt'. P3: Salt and Sea Salt only in the non-food area 'Bosun Locker' -> no badge on either row. The rules were cached in localStorage mbp_mpa_rules. The production bug is fixed.
action_items: Minor/optional: splitParts (split on , & and) runs BEFORE span noise is stripped in conceptsOf. So 'Tomatoes (finely chopped, drained) 200g' is split into 'Tomatoes (finely chopped' and 'drained)'. The '\(.*?\)' span then never matches, the key becomes 'tomatoes chopped', and there is no sub badge against 'Tinned plum tomatoes'. Fix: run the noise.spans replacement on the whole name before splitParts (e.g. in conceptsOf: splitParts(applySpans(name))). Reproduced in mpa_bidir_unit.mjs (the 'P EDGE' case).
critical_code_review_comments: compileNoise: patterns go to the 'patterns' bucket, are not anchored, and drop a token if they match anywhere in it. For example, '[0-9]+' drops any token that contains a digit, such as 'b12' or '7up'. This is acceptable for food names. Anchoring with ^...$ would be stricter.

The SAFE_WORD check only tests 'salt'. A pattern like '[a-r]+' or 'sa' would pass and could still remove real words. This is acceptable as a heuristic. Testing a few more sample words would make it more robust.
keyOf only makes the last word singular, so 'tomatoes chopped' never reaches the 'tomato' group. This is only relevant when noise stripping leaves extra words behind.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested scenarios (unit 27/28: only the extra edge case fails)

seed_data_creation: The Pro boat was seeded with scenarios P1/P2/P3, then restored from /tmp/pro_boat_59.json (fresh backup). Both private admin lists were deleted, and GET /api/admin/template-lists returns [].
